title: Day-1 rubric — the explicit criteria the reflective loop evaluates against
description: Graph Engineering §VI.A requires the Day-1 loop to carry 'an evaluator with explicit criteria'. This schema is what makes 'explicit' checkable: a rubric is a weighted set of criteria, each with BOTH a natural-language assertion (what the model judge is asked) and a deterministic detector (what CI can score with zero spend). The two heads are the paper's §VI.G evaluation plane — 'deterministic checks, model evaluators, and human review' — expressed as one object so a criterion can never be graded by prose alone.

skill.description: Directory name under skills/. MUST match the rubric's own directory (enforced by structural §48).

fixture.description: The task the skill is asked to perform. Day-1's precondition is an LLM call 'whose output can be evaluated' — this names what is being evaluated.

workspace.description: Repo-relative directory the skill runs against, or null when the fixture is prompt-only.

reference_drafts.description: SYNTHETIC drafts, hand-authored, used ONLY to prove the rubric discriminates without spending tokens. These are not measured skill output and may never be reported as one.

weak.description: A draft exhibiting the skill's known failure mode. Must score BELOW the discrimination floor.

strong.description: A draft doing the job correctly. Must score ABOVE the discrimination ceiling.

partial.description: OPTIONAL third reference: a draft that is mostly right and fails a named part of the job. Weak-vs-strong proves only that the rubric separates working from broken; a scorer that returns 0 for a 4-of-5 artifact passes that test and still cannot show a revision round anything to move. Required in practice for any rubric using `detector.rows` — structural §48 asserts its score lands strictly between the weak and strong reference scores.

seed.description: What the workspace starts with, before the skill writes anything. A STRING entry copies one file to its basename — the original meaning, kept so `task-executor`'s flat fixture does not move its fingerprint. The OBJECT form is required by any fixture seeding a TREE: the Tier-1 oracles resolve their inputs through lib/paths.mjs (`shapeup/<slug>/spec/usecases/`, `.shapeup/<slug>/tasks/`), so a seed flattened to its basename lands where the oracle does not look and every artifact scores 0 while the instrument reports itself healthy. `from` may be a file or a directory; a directory carries whole.

to.description: Workspace-relative destination. Defaults to the source's basename.

deliverable.description: What the skill is graded on producing, workspace-relative. A STRING for a single file (`todo.js`); an ARRAY when the artifact spans more than one path — `scope-architect` writes N contracts into a directory whose membership is its own decision, and `ba-pitch-analyzer` writes a spec tree AND a board, which live under two different storage roots (ADR-0001). Each path may be a file or a directory. This is the set carried between rounds and the set hashed for the no-improvement ratchet; a path left out of it is a path a revision round silently loses.

contract_files.description: Repo-relative files whose CONTENT defines what this fixture grades — the oracle's contract rows, the runner, the seeded spec. Used to compute the fixture fingerprint that decides whether a new measurement supersedes an older one or is comparable to it. List anything an author could edit to change the score of an unchanged deliverable; a contract JSON read at runtime by a listed script must be listed too, because hashing the script alone would miss a row being added to it.

discrimination.description: The selftest's pass condition. A rubric that cannot separate its own weak and strong reference drafts is not an instrument, so CI asserts the separation rather than the existence of the file.

stopping_rule.description: Day-1 requires a stopping rule. `approve_at` is the score at which the evaluator returns decision=approve; `max_rounds` is the paper's iteration_limit (its reflective_task default is 3).

grades.description: What artifact the rubric grades. 'work-result' = assert over the worker's typed output envelope (exact, phrasing-independent, and the shape the skill actually contracts to return). 'prose' = regex over free text, for skills with no structured contract; it measures format conformance as much as craft and should be treated as a fallback.

kind.description: must → satisfied when the detector fires. must_not → satisfied when it does NOT.

dimension.description: Grouping label so a score can be read per-dimension, not just as one number (paper Table III: 'average success hides catastrophic cases').

assertion.description: The model-judge head: the criterion in the words the judge is asked to rule on.

traces_to.description: Optional pointer to the artifact this criterion was derived from (e.g. an existing fixture's grade.must entry), so a rubric criterion is never invented free-hand.

Detector.description: Three heads. `oracle` delegates to a script that ALREADY grades this artifact (spec-lint, trace-lint, board-derive, the evaluation oracles) and is the Tier-1 default: zero authored criteria, so the rubric cannot inherit its author's blind spots. `json` asserts over a field of the worker's output envelope — exact, phrasing-independent. `regex` matches draft text and is the fallback of last resort: v1 of the spec-evaluator rubric was all-regex and scored a correct evaluation 0.429 on phrasing alone.

path.description: json head only. Dotted path into the envelope; a `[]` segment flattens an array (e.g. verdict.criteria[].evidence).

equals.description: json head: detected when any value at `path` equals this (case-insensitive).

matches.description: json head: detected when any value at `path` matches this regex.

min_count.description: json head: detected when `path` yields at least this many values.

cmd.description: oracle head only. Command to run; {{workspace}}, {{slug}} and {{root}} are substituted. Exit 0 = detected, 1 = not detected, 2 = usage error (ABORTS — a misconfigured oracle is a broken instrument, not a bad artifact). With `path`, the oracle's stdout is parsed as JSON and the path assertion applies instead of the exit code.

rows.description: oracle head only. Splits the oracle's report into per-row verdicts so the criterion scores as the FRACTION of rows passing instead of all-or-nothing. Without it, a deliverable failing one of five contract rows scores exactly the same as one that was never written — measured: fifteen consecutive rounds at 4-of-5, all recorded as 0.0, with no number a revision could move. `satisfied` still requires every row, so a stopping rule of approve_at 1.0 keeps its meaning; only the score becomes readable. Partial credit is honoured for `kind: must` ONLY — a part-violated prohibition is not part-satisfied.

pattern.description: Regex with NAMED groups: `status` (required), `id` and `label` (optional). Declared here rather than inferred by the scorer, because the row format belongs to the oracle: a guessed pattern would silently match nothing the day an oracle reworded its report, scoring every artifact 0 while looking healthy. Matching zero rows is therefore a hard error, not an empty result.

pass.description: The `status` group's value that means the row passed (e.g. "PASS").
